title: The norm characteristic polynomial for a finite locally free affine algebra
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital ring homomorphism, and suppose the affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite locally free of degree $r\ge0$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $N_\varphi:B\to A$ denote the canonical determinant norm, characterized by the determinant of the multiplication matrix on every local finite free chart. Write $\varphi[T]:A[T]\to B[T]$ for its coefficientwise polynomial extension [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The latter map is finite locally free of degree $r$ as well. For $b\in B$, put
$$
P_b(T)=N_{\varphi[T]}(T-b)\in A[T].
$$
This polynomial has the form $T^r+\sum_{j<r}a_jT^j$ with $a_j\in A$ and satisfies $\bigl(\varphi[T](P_b)\bigr)(b)=0$ in $B$. In particular it is monic of degree $r$ when $A\ne0$. If $A$ is the zero ring, the displayed form and annihilation assertion still hold. The norm and polynomial are defined by the local determinant characterization, independent of choices of local bases. No global freeness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First suppose $A=0$. Since $\varphi$ is unital, $1_B=\varphi(1_A)=\varphi(0_A)=0_B$, so $B=0$ too. Both polynomial rings are zero rings. There is a unique function $B\to A$ and a unique function $B[T]\to A[T]$; these satisfy every local determinant condition, since their spectra have no points. The polynomial extension has empty source and target, so the finite, flat, locally finitely presented and fibre-degree conditions are vacuous. Its unique polynomial equals $T^r+\sum_{j<r}0T^j$, and its value at the unique element of $B$ is zero. Henceforth assume $A\ne0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-principal-basis-cover] to $\varphi$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given degree-$r$ finite locally free hypothesis. Obtain $f_i$ generating the unit ideal of $A$, rank-$r$ bases of $B_{f_i}$, and the quasi-coherent pushforward and section identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-polynomial-basis-charts] with this cover. Thus $\varphi[T]$ is finite locally free of degree $r$, with quasi-coherent pushforward; $g_i=C(f_i)$ generate $A[T]$, and the localized polynomial algebras have the stated constant bases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-principal-free-algebra-determinant-norm] to $(R,D)=(A,B)$ and $(A[T],B[T])$, using respectively the covers $f_i$ and $g_i$ and their rank-$r$ bases. Using a separate characteristic-polynomial variable $Z$, it constructs both unique norms by $N(u)=(-1)^r\chi_u(0)$. For the polynomial pair the coefficient ring here is $A[T]$, so $Z$ is distinct from $T$. Its affine-chart clause applies to the quasi-coherent pushforwards already obtained, so these are precisely the locally characterized norms in the statement, independent of bases.

source.place: Tags 02DU (exercises-exercise-trace-det)(1) and 02DV (exercises-exercise-trace-det-rings)(1); Tag 09XI (more-algebra-lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof (3) implies (1), characteristic-polynomial gluing paragraph; old item proof steps 6-7.

proof.text: For $b\in B$, let $M_i(b)$ be its multiplication matrix in the basis from step 2. Under the coefficientwise localization maps and constant bases of [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-polynomial-basis-charts], multiplication by $T-C(b)$ has matrix $TI_r-M_i(b)$: its $k$th column comes from $Te_{i,k}-be_{i,k}$. By [lem-a1-principal-free-algebra-determinant-norm], the image of $N_{\varphi[T]}(v)$ is the determinant of multiplication by the image of $v$, for every $v\in B[T]$. Thus the exact local hypothesis of [lem-a1-principal-free-norm-polynomial-comparison] holds with $N_T=N_{\varphi[T]}$. Its conclusion gives $P_b=\chi_b=T^r+\sum_{j<r}a_jT^j$, annihilation after coefficient extension and evaluation at $b$, and monicity and degree $r$ for $A\ne0$. Its rank-zero clause gives $B=0$ and $P_b=1_A$; step 1 covers the zero base ring.

lean.statement: theorem finiteLocallyFree_norm_characteristicPolynomial {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (r : ℕ) (h : (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r) : (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ))).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r ∧ ∃ N : B → A, (IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm φ N ∧ ∀ N' : B → A, IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm φ N' → N' = N) ∧ ∃ Npoly : Polynomial B → Polynomial A, (IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ) Npoly ∧ ∀ Npoly' : Polynomial B → Polynomial A, IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ) Npoly' → Npoly' = Npoly) ∧ ∀ b : B, (∃ a : Fin r → A, Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) = Polynomial.X ^ r + ∑ j : Fin r, Polynomial.C (a j) * Polynomial.X ^ (j : ℕ)) ∧ (Polynomial.map φ (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b))).eval b = 0 ∧ (Nontrivial A → (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).Monic ∧ (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).natDegree = r)
lean.note: The theorem spells out unique existence of both norms from their local determinant characterization, together with polynomial base change, expansion, annihilation, and conditional monicity/degree. The two following definitions choose only these uniquely determined norm functions and form N_{φ[X]}(X-C b). The local determinant predicate is a helper for this owning node, not a replacement for the finite locally free hypothesis.
